content:
Apple announced plans to enable users to copy and paste content between iPhone and Windows computers, in response to Microsoft's interoperability request in the EU. Details below.

This feature may be limited to the EU region.

According to a MacRumors finding, Apple has added an entry to its EU interoperability request page, showing that the company has agreed to develop a solution that lets extensions share and import iPhone clipboard items with paired devices (including Windows computers).

In Microsoft's initial request submitted on March 25, 2026, the company pointed out that it is currently unable to offer a feature comparable to "Universal Clipboard," which lets users copy and paste between Apple devices.

Microsoft further asked Apple to provide ongoing clipboard access so that persistent syncing can take place between iPhone and Windows computers, and listed three main use cases:

Copy text or other supported content on an iPhone and paste it directly on a Windows computer, and vice versa. Complete typical workflows without having to bring an app to the foreground, or repeatedly manually initiating a transfer. Treat the clipboard sync experience as a lightweight, persistent feature rather than a manual, app-driven operation.

The company argued that "cross-device copy and paste is a fundamental productivity interaction that users expect to work seamlessly across their primary devices," adding that its goal is "not to replace or replicate Apple's system experience, but to achieve the basic level of cross-device productivity that users already expect when working across devices."

Apple responded on April 27, saying that after an initial assessment of Microsoft's request, it had decided to "move it forward to the next stage of the interoperability process."

Subsequently, on June 26, Apple confirmed it would develop a relevant solution and outlined its expected functionality.

The company also explained that Microsoft will need to rely on the AccessorySetupKit framework — the same framework that is at the centre of Meta's EU interoperability request, which aims to support AirPods-like pairing between iPhone and iPad.

In Microsoft's case, AccessorySetupKit will be used to obtain permission to share clipboard contents with a paired Windows computer, with users needing to authorise once per device.

Apple described the item as "a significant engineering undertaking" and said it plans to complete development by autumn 2027, after which a solution will first ship in a developer beta before being released publicly.

This timeline suggests the feature could debut with iOS 28, although Apple has not confirmed which software version it will be included in.
